notes:
POC focused on spike reliability and graceful degradation. Customer runs omnichannel CCaaS (voice + chat + SMS) — typical steady-state 1200 concurrent agents, seasonal peaks up to 32k active sessions (estimated). Key asks:
- 95th pct token latency target: < 300ms for single-turn agent-suggest; 99th pct fallback plan required.
- Throughput: sustain ~1.5k concurrent generation requests during spikes; burst to 6k for 10-30 minute windows.
- Cost sensitivity: wants predictable unit economics for seasonal events (Black Friday window). Prefer reserved/dedicated pricing but need auto-burst.
- Model preferences: open to Llama-derivative quantized variants; want ability to route to smaller quantized variant when under pressure.
- Reliability requirements: automatic fallback (model variant or region), queue backpressure handling, graceful degradation to cached suggestions.
- Security/compliance: must live in customer VPC (private control plane), data residency in US/EU, SSO + SCIM, per-request audit logs, KMS for key management.
Notes from CTO (Anika Rao): "We can tolerate some latency increase but cannot accept >2% failed intent extractions during peak — that breaks our escalation SLAs."
Short issues: legal needs DPA + security questionnaire answers; engineering wants a template of batching/caching config for their workload; ops wants a runbook for cascade failure scenarios.
Quick wins: run synthetic spike replay using their 2024 traffic trace (drive link above); provide dedicated pool sizing recommendation + burst policy; demo automatic model fallback to quantized variant.
Gmail threads referenced for legal and pricing. Fireflies ids for demo + kickoff attached. Jira INF-9823 is for kernel-level perf question we escalated to infra team.
